- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction to bearish signals.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% to prevent overcorrection.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in the short term (1–3 days) after a strong move; adjust forecast to reflect gradual return to historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period reversals; if sentiment turns negative mid-horizon, reduce forecast slope toward end of period.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to anticipate sentiment shifts 1–2 days ahead.
